01 Admin Quickstart: Copilot CoE install

Run these steps one at a time in PowerShell 7.4 or later, as required by the kit scripts and PnP.PowerShell 3.2.0. Keep the customer’s organization folder outside the kit folder; that way, updating the kit later will not overwrite the customer’s settings.

Two important rules:

  • For a brand-new install, do not use -ResumeExisting. It is only for finishing an interrupted install.

  • “Where should users report accidentally sharing sensitive data or another security/privacy incident involving Copilot?”

    Before a customer installation, put the organization’s approved reporting-page URL in its Deployment-Settings.json, for example:

    "Links": {
  "DataSafetyIncident": "https://your-organization.service-now.com/security-report"
}

    That is an illustrative address, not a working destination. Use an existing approved security-reporting form or instructions page—you don’t necessarily need to create anything new.

    If this setting is empty, the installer asks STOP / PROCEED before creating tenant resources; STOP is the default. An explicit PROCEED is for a reviewed lab or pilot and leaves a visible “route not configured” notice. It does not supply an incident-reporting service. A nonempty invalid URL remains a hard stop. Configure an approved working route before production.

Screenshot guide: The pictures below are from an internal content-demo tenant used to validate the kit, captured October 16, 2026. Red rectangles identify the affected areas. They do not mean every boxed area should be edited directly in SharePoint: follow the source-file and update instructions beside each picture.

Use the listed page or list path on your own CoE site. The pictures are embedded in this HTML file and remain available offline.

Captions name the default headings shown in the pictures. Your organization’s overrides may rename or remove those headings. Locate the page by its URL and identify its configured source; do not expect customized sites to repeat the screenshot wording.

01Extract the kit and create the organization folder

First, choose where the customer’s organization folder will live. This folder controls the site’s wording, governance drafts, learning paths, and the starting prompts in the Copilot Prompt Library.

If someone already gave you a completed organization folder, copy that folder instead of creating a new one.

Customer typeFolder to copyPrompts included
Higher educationOrg-Template230 higher-education prompts, included by default
State/local government, commercial or GCC Moderate — not GCC High or DoDContentPacks\Government-StateLocal230 general government prompts; higher-education prompts are excluded

Content pack is not cloud acceptance. LearningEnvironment: Government selects government content; it does not select or prove GCC Moderate behavior. Confirm the actual target cloud separately. A Government-content run in a commercial lab is commercial evidence, not GCC Moderate acceptance. GCC High and DoD are unsupported.

Choose one frozen release ZIP before you begin. Use the master ZIP or an identical customer copy named in its release receipt; verify that ZIP’s SHA256 against the receipt. An older versioned folder is history, not an automatically updated copy. The authoring source and an extracted working folder are not release ZIPs. Renaming an old ZIP does not upgrade it.

Use commands like this:

$zip = 'C:\CoE-Releases\Copilot-CoE-Implementation-Kit.zip'
$expectedHash = '<paste SHA256 from the release receipt>'
$installRoot = 'C:\CoE-Install\Contoso'
$kitRoot = Join-Path $installRoot '03_Build\CopilotCoE-Kit'
$orgPath = 'C:\CoE-Orgs\Contoso'

if ($expectedHash -notmatch '^[0-9A-Fa-f]{64}$' -or
    (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $expectedHash) {
    throw 'The chosen release ZIP does not match its receipt.'
}
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $installRoot) { throw 'Use a fresh extraction folder for a clean install.' }
Expand-Archive -LiteralPath $zip -DestinationPath $installRoot
Set-Location $kitRoot

# Only when starting a NEW organization folder; do not overwrite a completed one.
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $orgPath) { throw 'Review the existing organization folder before using it.' }
Copy-Item .\Org-Template $orgPath -Recurse

# Government — use this instead of the line above:
# Copy-Item .\ContentPacks\Government-StateLocal $orgPath -Recurse

If you received a completed organization folder, point $orgPath to it instead of copying a template. When adapting a prior validation profile for a new site, copy only reviewed settings, Content and approved Assets into a fresh folder. Do not copy CoE-Revision-Report.json, CoE-Removal-Manifest.json or RevisionAudit from another deployment; those files identify its old Team and site.

Then open the settings file:

notepad (Join-Path $orgPath 'Deployment-Settings.json')

In that file, set:

  • Tenant details.
  • The owner’s UPN.
  • A fresh MailNickname for this site and the intended DisplayName. Keep the alias in this file aligned with the install command: the updater and remover read it later. The installer rejects an active or recycled alias collision.
  • The organization name.
  • The support mailbox.
  • The organization’s email domains.
  • Keep TeamVisibility set to Private.
  • Fill in real HTTPS addresses for Links.ServiceDesk, TechnologyRequest, AIGuidelines, and DataSafetyIncident.
  • For government deployments, replace every <placeholder> and set TimeZone — for example, Central Standard Time.

Optional: add the customer’s own prompts

The Prompt Library starts with the base prompts included in the folder you copied.

To add the customer’s own prompts, put CSV files here:

$orgPath\Content\OrgPrompts

Use the same CSV format used by the Microsoft 365 admin center:

Title,Description,Display Prompt,Prompt Text,Products,Department,Task Type,Locale

These are the same files you would upload through Copilot > Prompts > Import.

How the kit treats the files:

  • A new CSV file name adds new prompts.
  • A CSV with the same name as a base file replaces that base file.
  • An empty CSV with a base file’s name removes that base prompt set.
  • The kit does not modify your CSV files.

Prompt CSVs are not filtered for DEMO/SAMPLE; remove demo rows before a Customer install. Review both the base prompt files and the organization’s CSVs. Prompts seeded from these files are inserted approved in Customer mode as well as Demo mode; the DEMO/SAMPLE asset-file filter does not protect the prompt list.

For an existing deployment, changing mode or removing a CSV does not automatically remove matching live prompts. Review and remove any existing demo prompt rows separately through the authorized list-management process.

To turn off the Prompt Library entirely, set "PromptLibrary": "Off".

For the on-site location and an example of the environment-specific prompt sets, see the Prompt Library screenshot in step 05.

02Register or update the provisioning app

A person approved to consent to app permissions runs this once per tenant. Afterward, they should confirm in Entra that every required permission shows as Granted.

Set-Location $kitRoot

Install-Module PnP.PowerShell -RequiredVersion 3.2.0 -Scope CurrentUser

.\01_Register-CoEProvisioningApp.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath

Before moving on, check that the Entra app permissions are granted, including the delegated User.Read.All permission.

If consent changed after someone previously signed in, add -ForceAuthentication to the install command in the next step.

Posting the three welcome messages currently works with the app’s existing delegated Group.ReadWrite.All, which Microsoft Graph supports only for backward compatibility. The recommended future posting scope is ChannelMessage.Send; changing consent is a separate reviewed app change. The kit does not request tenant-wide ChannelMessage.Read.All just to silence a test warning: without it, step 05’s visual post check is mandatory.

03Run the clean install

A SharePoint and Teams administrator runs this after the settings file and app consents are ready.

GCC Moderate / switching tenants: confirm the sign-in

When switching between commercial and GCC Moderate tenants, or when the browser offers the wrong cached account, add -AuthenticationMode Interactive -ForceAuthentication to the installer command below. Sign in with an approved administrator account for the target tenant.

-ForceAuthentication requests a fresh interactive sign-in; it is optional, not a GCC requirement. Also use it after app permissions or consent change. It does not select the tenant: confirm Tenant, AdminFQDN, SiteFQDN, and PnPClientID in the target organization’s Deployment-Settings.json first.

Do not combine -ForceAuthentication with -AuthenticationMode DeviceLogin. This kit supports commercial and GCC Moderate tenants, not GCC High or DoD.

Set-Location $kitRoot

.\02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 `
  -OrgPath $orgPath `
  -ContentMode Customer `
  -SeedDemoContent

If $orgPath\Assets has files, the installer lists them and asks which categories to host. Add -AcceptOrgAssets only after reviewing every eligible file and approving all of them; it is not a safe generic default. Do not grant visitors or loosen sharing merely to complete an install.

The welcome posts are attributed to the account running this command. Use an approved CoE-owner or dedicated provisioning administrator identity, not an individual’s personal admin identity, when that attribution matters.

-ContentMode Customer is the production setting: no generated demo disclaimer or seeded sample calendar events. Organization asset files whose names contain DEMO or SAMPLE as a whole word are filtered out instead of offered for hosting; prompt CSV rows are not covered by that filter. Use -ContentMode Demo only for an internal sales/content-demo site, never for a customer-facing install. -SeedDemoContent is required either way — omitting it skips all page, catalog, and calendar content regardless of -ContentMode, leaving only the Team and an empty SharePoint site.

"SampleNotice": "none" means no notice, not the literal word “none” on a page. Customer mode suppresses configured sample notices regardless of that setting. Demo mode requires a nonempty resolved notice; a blank setting uses the default sample notice, while none is invalid for Demo mode.

STOP / PROCEED is a lab decision, not production acceptance

The installer and updater ask about lab-looking support mailboxes, missing support routes, a default Demo notice, long titles, parent-Team guest/out-of-domain members and fallback headers. Decisions are saved beside settings in CoE-Advisory-Decisions.json, tied to the tenant, site host, Team alias and exact advisory facts. An unchanged decision is reused with a visible message; a saved STOP remains a stop until the configuration or decision is deliberately changed.

The checker remains read-only: it never prompts for or saves a decision. In Customer mode, a lab-looking support mailbox or a saved target-scoped LabSupportMailbox PROCEED produces a WARN, even after the mailbox setting changes. Confirm its owner and monitoring, replace lab addresses before production, and review obsolete saved approvals. A saved PROCEED does not waive this manual-review gate or any identity, governance, tenant or sharing check.

Which version is installed? Use the extracted ZIP’s root VERSION.txt for the kit release version. The version values inside the base and Government CoE-Revision-Content.json files identify their content revisions and are also written to the deployment report; they can differ from the packaged release version. Do not identify the release from those JSON values or relabel them just to make the numbers match.

Using an organization-provided launcher? A short pwsh -NoProfile -File "Start-CoE-Install.ps1" command runs that launcher, which can pass the full argument list internally. Confirm that it calls 02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 with the intended -OrgPath, -ContentMode, and -SeedDemoContent; use -AcceptOrgAssets only if the assets were reviewed and approved. The launcher is not a different installer; no launcher is required for the direct command above.

A first install usually takes about 25–35 minutes. Creating the 230 base prompts accounts for roughly 5–10 minutes of that.

For a clean install:

  • Do not add -ResumeExisting.
  • For a fresh sign-in, follow the red callout above. If the Team/site was already created before a failure, follow the recovery steps below; -ForceAuthentication does not make another clean install safe.

If the install fails

Do not immediately start another clean install, and do not automatically delete or purge resources.

  1. Read the transcript files here: 
    $orgPath\RevisionAudit\*-transcript.txt
  2. Fix the underlying problem.
  3. Confirm that the existing Team and SharePoint site have the exact intended identity.
  4. Only then use -ResumeExisting to finish that same build.

If you are validating a changed version of the kit, use a new site alias or perform a separately reviewed removal and fresh install. Using -ResumeExisting does not prove that a new kit version works.

If you choose to purge and rebuild

Purging permanently removes the Team, its conversations, the primary site and the reviewed related channel sites. Back up the whole organization folder and export any live content you need first. Keep the original deployment identity records until cleanup is complete. Use the official remover, not a site-only manual delete that can leave the group or channel sites behind.

# Preview the exact permanent-removal plan first.
.\04_Remove-CopilotCoE.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Purge -WhatIf

# Only after approving that plan; type the requested alias and exact URLs.
.\04_Remove-CopilotCoE.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Purge

Do not rebuild until the result says AliasReusable : True. If cleanup is incomplete, retain the identity records and follow the named error or wait before rerunning the remover. Then verify the intended ZIP’s hash, extract to a new empty folder, and run step 03 without -ResumeExisting, followed separately by step 04. Preserve the earlier extraction and logs for troubleshooting.

No reset is required by the standard numbered scripts, either before purge or after a completed purge. They do not read Customer-Walkthrough-State.json. The remover’s CoE-Purge-Receipt.json records cleanup evidence; it is not a prerequisite for a direct 02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 run.

Organization-specific launchers are separate. A launcher supplied outside this kit may keep an InstallAttempted flag and provide -ResetAfterPurge. That reset belongs only to that launcher and occurs after verified cleanup, never before purge. Follow its own recovery contract, or use the standard numbered scripts directly. For an older or manual purge with no receipt, have an administrator review live and recycled resources; do not fabricate a receipt, replace identity records or manually toggle state to force a retry.

04Check the result

The install is not accepted until automated checks and every required manual review pass. This script reads the site; it does not change anything. Use the actual site address printed at the end of step 03, not the example host below.

Step 03 does not automatically run this checker. Run the following block separately after installation, and again after every content update, using the checker from the same extracted release.

$siteUrl = 'https://contoso.sharepoint.com/sites/CopilotCoE'

Set-Location $kitRoot

.\Test-CoEInstall.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -SiteUrl $siteUrl -ContentMode Customer

Pass the same -ContentMode used for install: Customer unlocks the Customer-mode checks (no sample rows, no demo text, and the Home “No sessions scheduled yet” placeholder when the calendar is empty). For a reviewed internal demonstration, pass -ContentMode Demo to both commands. Omitting Customer here silently skips its checks.

Automated checks succeeded when its final line starts with:

ALL CHECKS PASSED

The script appends a count, such as ALL CHECKS PASSED (277); the count varies with mode and applicable checks. Demo-only notice-presence checks do not run in Customer mode, which instead checks for notice leaks. Do not require a previous run’s exact count. This is not the whole acceptance gate if any check says WARN. The result then adds MANUAL REVIEW REQUIRED. Read each warning and capture its specific evidence: a 1366px site screenshot for a header-layout or long-title/menu-overflow warning, an actual Teams channel-post inspection when message reading is denied, or the support owner’s confirmation and a reviewed production route for a lab-mailbox warning. Link checks compare configured destinations; they do not prove an endpoint works or is monitored. Do not grant ChannelMessage.Read.All solely to suppress that warning.

If any line says FAIL, it names the problem. Send that output, along with the run log, to whoever is troubleshooting the install.

For an internal end-to-end validation of the full repair path, after the first check and the manual welcome-post review, run the following on the same new site, then repeat this test and step 05. -RepairCapturedPages can replace customized captured-page content, so use it on a fresh validation site or only after a reviewed repair decision:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All -RepairCapturedPages -ContentMode Customer
.\Test-CoEInstall.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -SiteUrl $siteUrl -ContentMode Customer

05Before readers see it

Before opening the site to regular users:

  • Add at least one non-owner test account as a member or reader, then do acceptance testing as that user.
  • Open General, Ask Us Anything and Share Your Prompt in Teams. Confirm exactly one prepared welcome post exists in each, its links work, and Customer-mode posts contain no sample notice. Check again after a repair update. The provisioning app can send posts but cannot read them without ChannelMessage.Read.All; ALL CHECKS PASSED with a Teams WARN does not replace this manual review. If an interrupted install left a post missing, visually confirm the exact missing channel before using 02_Install-CopilotCoE.ps1 -ResumeExisting -PublishWelcomeToChannels 'General' (substitute only the channels verified missing). Repeating that option can create duplicates.
  • Approve and feature one Agent Showcase entry so you can test both the empty and populated reader layouts.
  • Open Training > Prompt library, then follow its link to the list, or open Copilot Prompt Library from Site contents (Lists/CopilotPromptLibrary/Prompts.aspx). Confirm the actual list contains the intended prompt sets. Government sites must not show higher-education prompts.
  • If reviewers are configured, manage them in the CoE Catalog Reviewers SharePoint group. With no configured reviewers, a fresh install does not create that group. To create it, add approved reviewers to CatalogReviewerUPNs and run a reviewed Guides/All update. Keep settings and live membership aligned: updates add configured reviewers back, but removing a name from settings does not remove the live member.

Reviewer-group illustration: No group-management screenshot is included here. The kit creates the CoE Catalog Reviewers group and the CoE Catalog Reviewer permission level only when CatalogReviewerUPNs lists at least one reviewer. Both starter templates have an empty reviewer list, so a fresh default install creates neither. Add approved reviewers to Deployment-Settings.json and run a reviewed Guides/All update to create them. Emptying the setting later does not delete an existing group or remove its members; inspect the actual group through the site’s permissions settings.

Use the update script only for reviewed changes. This example is for a Customer-mode deployment; use -ContentMode Demo instead for a demo. Omitting the parameter defaults to Customer and can change notices and sample data.

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All -ContentMode Customer

After any update, run step 04 again.

06Customizing content after install

There are several kinds of content, and they behave differently when the update script runs again. This matters because an edit made in the wrong place can either disappear during the next update or never apply at all.

Before using SharePoint’s Edit button: identify what owns the content

Generated page wording belongs in the organization folder. Live catalog entries belong in SharePoint lists. Editing the wrong surface can lose a change or leave the published page unchanged. The red rectangles in the screenshots identify an element; they are not instructions to edit it in SharePoint.

What you want to changeWhere to make the lasting changeWhat happens next
The italic demo notice, organization wording, or configured support linksDeployment-Settings.json in the organization folderRun the reviewed content update in the correct mode; Home and the captured-page notices need deliberate -RepairCapturedPages. See A and D.
Guide instructions or the introduction/body of a generated section pageThe matching source under $orgPath\Content-Scope Guides or All rebuilds these pages. SharePoint text edits are replaced. See B.
An agent description, owner, Featured flag, learning row, prompt, champion, or calendar eventThe actual SharePoint list item, not the page displaying itUse the list’s review/approval workflow where enabled. Existing rows are generally preserved rather than overwritten from seed files. See F.
A governance Word draftEdit the published document with its authorized reviewers; reconcile the organization source before a later updateA differing managed draft is not silently overwritten: a Governance/All update can stop until the difference is reviewed. See C.
A hosted reference fileReview the live document and matching source under $orgPath\AssetsThe kit replaces an existing hosted copy only with -ReplaceOrgAssets. See E.
A new organization-owned page outside the kit’s managed page namesSharePoint page editingThe kit does not generate that page’s body. It can still manage site navigation, header settings, and page comments; do not assume the whole site is hands-off.

Before using the commands below, select the mode that matches the deployment. Do not change mode merely to change wording:

Set-Location $kitRoot
$contentMode = 'Customer'  # Use 'Demo' for an existing demo deployment.

Confirm $orgPath, $kitRoot, and the existing site alias first. The updater reads MailNickname from the organization settings; if it is stale, pass -MailNickname with the existing alias. Do not invent a new alias to update or rename a site.

A. Single settings — AI policy URL, document list, org name, notice text

These include:

  • Links.AIGuidelines — the configured AI policy route, rendered in the generated support block and in page sources that use its link token.
  • GovernanceLinks — the links rendered where the Governance page source includes {{LinkList:GovernanceLinks}}. The default source calls that area “Official documents”; an override may rename it.
  • TrainingLinks — the links rendered where the Training and Enablement source includes {{LinkList:TrainingLinks}}. The default heading is “Self-paced resources”; an override may rename it.
  • OrgName — your organization’s name in the welcome text.
  • OrgNoun — the word used for the organization, such as “company,” “agency,” or “university.”
  • SampleNotice — the repeated italic notice on generated pages in Demo mode, including the line beneath the Agent Showcase introduction. Home and captured-page notices are covered separately in section D.

To change any of these, edit the settings file:

notepad (Join-Path $orgPath 'Deployment-Settings.json')

Change the value, save the file, then run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All -ContentMode $contentMode
These settings are the source of the generated elements, not live links into SharePoint. Saving JSON alone changes no page. A Guides/All update replaces the generated page text; it does not refresh Home’s welcome and notice unless you deliberately add -RepairCapturedPages.

Keep the binding in a customized source. Use {{LinkList:GovernanceLinks}} wherever you want the settings-driven policy list, and {{Link:AIGuidelines|AI guidelines}} for the settings-driven policy link. Links typed as literal URLs in the source remain independent of those settings; changing JSON cannot update a hardcoded citation.

Replace the demo notice with your organization’s own wording

The text does not have to use the kit’s exact demo phrase. For an existing demo, edit just SampleNotice inside its Deployment-Settings.json; keep the tenant, alias, and other settings. For example, this is custom wording for a demonstration, not a production-policy statement:

"SampleNotice": "Demonstration for review. Use only public or synthetic data; not official agency policy."

To refresh generated public pages such as Agent Showcase while preserving Home’s welcome and the captured-page notices:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope Guides -ContentMode Demo

To apply the changed notice to Home, the captured pages, and other All-scope content too, review the reset effects in section D first, then use:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All -ContentMode Demo -RepairCapturedPages

Demo requires a non-empty notice. A blank or omitted SampleNotice uses the default sample wording; "none" requests no notice and is rejected in Demo mode.

Customer mode ignores SampleNotice. An approved production deployment uses -ContentMode Customer, which suppresses the generated demo notice and changes sample-seeding/cleanup behavior. It is not a cosmetic switch for a lab or a certification that the site is production-ready. Existing captured notices still need a reviewed repair, and hardcoded sample wording in organization sources needs separate review. Put any required permanent production wording in the appropriate organization page sources instead; do not use SampleNotice as a production-banner field.

These commands publish site changes. Back up and review the affected content first, then run Test-CoEInstall.ps1 with the same -ContentMode. No update is performed merely by reading this guide.

The site/Team title is a different element. DisplayName supplies the deployment title; this content updater does not rename an existing Team or SharePoint site. Use the supported SharePoint/Teams administration process for a reviewed rename, keep the settings aligned for future builds, and do not change MailNickname expecting it to rename an existing site URL.

B. Guide and section page wording

This covers pages such as:

  • “Start in 10 minutes.”
  • The Service Catalog table.
  • The Governance page body.
  • Other numbered section pages.

-Scope Guides and -Scope All rebuild these generated page bodies. -Scope Governance does not rebuild the public guide/section pages; it handles the restricted governance workrooms. There is no per-page preservation switch in the public content updater.

A direct SharePoint edit to one of these generated bodies is replaced when that page is rebuilt on the next Guides/All update, even if the reason for the update is adding a prompt or changing a setting.

Create the override before editing it. The higher-education Org-Template supplies instructions and folders, not ready-to-edit guide overrides. A path in the table below may not exist yet. Copy the matching starter file under $orgPath\Content and edit that copy, not the shared kit.

For example, copy the higher-education starter from $kitRoot\SeedContent without overwriting an existing override:

$rel = 'Guides\00a-Start-in-10-Minutes.md'
$target = Join-Path $orgPath "Content\$rel"
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $target) {
    Write-Host "Existing override retained; edit this file: $target"
} else {
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path -Parent $target) | Out-Null
    Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path $kitRoot "SeedContent\$rel") -Destination $target
}

For Government deployments, use the matching source under $kitRoot\ContentPacks\Government-StateLocal\Content where present; otherwise use $kitRoot\SeedContent. Preserve the original relative path and filename.

To change this pageEdit this file
Start in 10 minutes$orgPath\Content\Guides\00a-Start-in-10-Minutes.md
Agent Showcase page title, summary, and static body$orgPath\Content\Sections\06-Agent-Showcase.md, unless the section configuration selects another file
Governance page body$orgPath\Content\Sections\03-Governance-and-Responsible-AI.md
Service Catalog and Support body$orgPath\Content\Sections\04-Service-Catalog-and-Support.md by default; check the section configuration first
FAQ answers$orgPath\Content\Copilot-FAQs.md
Data protection page body$orgPath\Content\Experience\Data-Protection.md

Keep source filenames exactly as shipped: 00a-Start-in-10-Minutes.md becomes the published page Guide-Start-in-10-Minutes.aspx. The source is not named after that page URL.

For section pages, check Content\Sections\Sections.json if your organization supplies it. Each section’s page identifies the SharePoint page and file selects the source filename under Content\Sections. An organization can select a different filename; editing the unused default file will not change that page.

The source’s first # heading becomes the page title, and its first > line becomes the summary. Change the repeated Demo notice through SampleNotice, not by copying the same disclaimer into every page source.

Keep settings and hosted-file tokens in the source

In Markdown (.md) page overrides, retain the tokens that you want to stay settings-driven. You can move a token or change its visible label; deleting it disconnects that part of the page without an error. It does not change the setting, delete an uploaded file, or create a replacement link.

TokenWhat it supplies
{{Link:<Key>|label}}, for example {{Link:DataSafetyIncident|Report an incident}}The corresponding Links.* destination and link label. Deleting the incident token removes that inline incident link; keep the separate reporting route visible and do not assume another page’s support block replaces it.
{{IfRouteMissing:<Key>|text}}Fallback instructions shown when that support route is not configured. Keep the safeguard along with the link token; it is removed automatically when the route is configured.
{{LinkList:GovernanceLinks}}The policy/reference links in GovernanceLinks.
{{LinkList:TrainingLinks}}The resources in TrainingLinks.
{{HostedFiles}}The links to hosted reference files on a section page. Deleting it hides those generated links even though the upload can still happen and the files remain in SharePoint.
{{MailTo:subject}}A mailto destination using SupportEmail and the stated subject.
{{OrgName}} and {{OrgNoun}}Organization-specific wording from the settings.

Replace <Key> with a real supported key such as DataSafetyIncident or ServiceDesk; do not paste the angle-bracket pattern literally. Route, link-list, and mailto macros are expanded in .md sources. The section’s hosted-file placeholder is handled separately, including when its selected source filename uses .txt.

Keep CSV prompt placeholders separate: {{...}} inside OrgPrompts files belongs to the person using the prompt and is deliberately not resolved by the installer.

Then run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope Guides -ContentMode $contentMode

Or, to update everything:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope All -ContentMode $contentMode
Do not hand-edit a kit-generated page body in SharePoint and expect that edit to survive a Guides/All update. Save the approved wording in the organization’s matching source file. Catalog rows are different: edit those in the actual list, as described in section F.

Not every label has a settings field. For example, the generated Agent Showcase headings “Featured agents” and “All approved agents,” and their generated explanatory text, are currently authored in the kit code. The section source changes the static introduction, not those strings. Request a supported kit enhancement if those labels must change; inventing a JSON property or editing the rendered web part is not a durable configuration method.

C. Governance Word documents

Governance documents behave the opposite way from guide and section pages.

The kit compares the text of a managed governance Word document with its source draft. An unchanged document is kept. If they differ and -ReplaceFiles is absent, the update stops rather than silently replacing the document. This can happen during -Scope Governance or All; Guides skips the governance documents.

To update a governance draft:

Edit the file under:

$orgPath\Content\Governance\...

Replacement is scoped to the whole run, not one edited draft

-ReplaceFiles authorizes replacement of every differing managed governance draft touched by that run, not only the draft you intended to change. Reconcile all reviewer-edited drafts first.

The kit generates a new Word document from the source text. Its generated styles and links are rebuilt; the published document’s custom formatting and reviewer comments are not carried over. The same switch also recycles matching legacy copies such as Sample-guidance.txt, and eligible earlier kit-generated draft documents in the managed folders. It is not limited to an in-place text correction.

With -Scope All it can also re-upload kit sample files in the public section folders. -Scope Guides -ReplaceFiles can re-upload those section files too, although it skips governance drafts. Organization asset replacement remains controlled separately by -ReplaceOrgAssets.

Before replacement, preserve an independent copy and check SharePoint version history and recycle-bin recovery options. Use version history for rollback where versions are retained; the kit’s extracted-text audit copies are not a full-document restore.

Run:

.\03_Update-CoEContent.ps1 -OrgPath $orgPath -Scope Governance -ContentMode $contentMode -ReplaceFiles

Authorized reviewers can edit the published Word document in SharePoint or Word. Reconcile those approved changes with the source before a later Governance/All update; do not promise editors that an ordinary rerun will ignore a difference.

Before using -ReplaceFiles, back up the published document and compare it with the intended source. The script records the prior extracted text in the kit’s RevisionAudit folder; this is not a full-fidelity backup of the original Word file, formatting, and comments.

A stopped update can leave some changes already published

In an All run, guide, section, and catalog content publishes before the governance-document comparison. If that comparison stops the run, those earlier changes are already live; the script does not roll them back. The deployment report is written only at the end, so an existing CoE-Revision-Report.json can still describe an earlier successful run.

Use -Scope Guides for changes that do not need governance-document processing. After any stopped run, preserve its transcript and before-copies, inspect the affected site content, and rerun Test-CoEInstall.ps1 with the correct site and content mode. An old report or a partially updated page is not proof that the run completed. Do not automatically purge or reinstall.

Keep both audit locations

RecordLocation when an organization folder is supplied
Run transcripts$orgPath\RevisionAudit\*-transcript.txt; without a valid organization folder, logging falls back to the kit’s RevisionAudit
Page and governance before-copies$kitRoot\RevisionAudit
Last completed deployment report$orgPath\CoE-Revision-Report.json

Copy the kit’s RevisionAudit folder to your private deployment records before replacing or deleting a working kit extraction, and retain the organization’s transcripts too. These files can contain actual site content; they are deployment records, not redistributable kit assets. The release packager omits runtime audit folders and rejects a ZIP containing RevisionAudit or deployment-report entries; do not distribute a used build directory as a kit.

Why there is no Word screenshot here: no governance Word-document screenshot is included. This is not evidence that your deployment lacks drafts: managed governance drafts live in the restricted Leadership Governance and Program Governance workrooms, not the public section’s reference-file folder. Open the actual document in your deployment; editing the public Governance page or its reference links does not edit a Word file.

D. Home and the four captured pages

These pages are special:

  • TrainingHome.aspx
  • Adoption-Best-Practices.aspx
  • Meet-your-ProjectTeam.aspx
  • Technical Readiness.aspx
  • Copilot-on-Microsoft-Mechanics.aspx

An ordinary update preserves Home’s custom welcome and the captured pages’ managed notice/breadcrumb text rather than performing the full repair. It is not a promise that no site element changes: updates can maintain calendar controls, remove obsolete Technical Readiness links, rebuild managed navigation/header settings, and disable page comments.

-RepairCapturedPages deliberately regenerates the following managed elements. Use it with -Scope Guides or All, never Governance, and review the impact first.

-RepairCapturedPages resets:

  • Home’s generated welcome/notice block, page title, Copilot tools, Explore tiles, champion link, and managed calendar area.
  • The four captured pages’ managed headers, certain page titles, breadcrumbs, and notice blocks.
  • The Microsoft Mechanics page body, which is rewritten with the kit’s official resource links.

It replaces direct SharePoint customizations to those specific elements with whatever the settings file and kit content generate.

Use OrgName, OrgNoun, and, in Demo mode, SampleNotice to change the generated Home wording, then apply a reviewed repair. Those settings do not provide an arbitrary free-text Home introduction. A direct SharePoint customization to the managed welcome block can survive an ordinary update but will be replaced by a later repair. Preserve approved custom wording before authorizing one.

Home: the Home picture in section A identifies the welcome elements with numbered callouts. The Copilot tools tiles and Explore the CoE tiles have no callout there; check them directly on your site after a repair. Each captured-page picture below identifies its breadcrumb with a numbered callout; they do not show the repair’s entire scope. In particular, the Microsoft Mechanics page body is also rewritten.

E. Uploaded reference documents

Guides/All updates offer section reference files from the configured asset categories, including:

$orgPath\Assets\Training
$orgPath\Assets\Service-Catalog
$orgPath\Assets\Agents
$orgPath\Assets\RAI-Policies
$orgPath\Assets\Success-Stories
$orgPath\Assets\Roadmap

Assets\Top10 is handled by -Scope All for the Top 10 tab. A Governance-only update does not process the public section asset folders.

During a run, the script asks whether to host them. You can answer the prompt, or pass -AcceptOrgAssets to accept automatically.

In Customer mode, a file whose name contains DEMO or SAMPLE (as a whole word) is filtered out and never offered for hosting, even with -AcceptOrgAssets. Confirm that a file really is approved customer content before removing a leftover sample label; do not rename demo material merely to bypass this safeguard.

An already-hosted file is left alone unless you pass -ReplaceOrgAssets. Review the changed file first, then use that switch if you want the new version published.

F. Lists and catalog entries: edit the data in SharePoint

When a page shows a List web part, use Open the list and edit the row there. Editing the surrounding page text does not change an agent’s description, owner, access requirements, or approval. A list approval is publication approval, not security approval or access to an agent’s sources.

Live contentWhere to editWhat a later update does
Agent entries, owners, sources, Featured, and retirementCopilot Agent Showcase listPreserves matching existing rows and publication state. Review and approve changes through native content approval.
Learning steps and ownershipCopilot Learning Paths listAdds missing LearningId rows; editing an already-seeded ID in Learning-Paths.json does not overwrite its live row.
Prompt wordingCopilot Prompt Library list; also maintain the organization CSV source for future deploymentsSeeds are insert-only by Title + Locale. A changed CSV does not replace an existing matching prompt. Newly seeded prompts are inserted approved; site-added prompts use the review workflow. See the DEMO/SAMPLE prompt warning before using Customer mode.
Session dates, registration links, and approvalCopilot Training Calendar listKeeps matching existing titles/dates; does not refresh a row from a changed CSV. Demo can recycle obsolete unapproved sample rows; Customer removes sample-prefixed sessions.
Champion appointments and contact informationDepartment Champions listPreserves existing matching directory rows. Appoint real people only after approval; seed categories are not appointments.
Success-story text and evidenceCopilot Success Stories listPreserves existing stories; new submissions, revisions, and retirements need the list’s approval workflow.

These preservation rules concern row content, not the whole list configuration. The kit can still maintain fields, views, approval settings, and catalog permissions. Keep the approved seed sources aligned for future deployments, and review mode-dependent cleanup before changing modes.

Included guide versus external overview: this HTML file is the administrator customization reference shipped with the kit. The public overview is a visual tour, may show an earlier site layout, and is not required to perform these steps. Updating this local guide does not update an already-released ZIP or publish a website; those are separate release actions.
